evidence: Auct. de Limit. p. 257 Goes.: pentagōniī ratiō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Greek πεντάγωνον, found as a noun only in the land surveyors’ writings (late). Lewis & Short has the adjective pentagōnius or pentagōnus without a classical citation. For a child the plain description is as good, on Columella’s model for the hexagon: figūra quīnque angulōrum (see the examples).

evidence: Prisc. Pond. p. 1358 P.; Boëth. Geom. p. 398 (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Haec figūra quīnque angulōrum est: pentagōnium.
phrases.english: This figure has five corners: it’s a pentagon.

phrases.latin: Quot latera habet? Quīnque, ut digitī manūs.
phrases.english: How many sides has it? Five, like the fingers of a hand.

sources: Lewis & Short: pentagonius · Lewis & Short: quinquangulus
